thread:
Carlos Mendez: saw a customer report where client hedging + gateway-local retry + fastpath->slowpath demote led to two deliveries and we exhausted a tenant's retry budget. want to propose a surface that helps downstreams dedupe and also lets us enforce retry budgets cleanly.
Omar Khan: curious about the trace. was gateway and client both retrying?
Carlos Mendez: short trace:
```
CLIENT: fires hedged request A and B nearly simultaneously (no Idempotency-Key)
EDGE: accepts A on fastpath, demotes to slowpath at t=2.1s; gateway fires local retry B to upstream as failover
UPSTREAM: ACK for A, then TCP reset; client B also delivered -> duplicate side-effect
```
Meera Patel: two problems: 1) lack of retry origin visibility for consumers; 2) no way to charge/limit combined hedges+gateway retries via a single budget.
Sasha Ivanov: proposal sketch: 1) gateway emits `X-Edge-Retry-Origin: gateway|client|hedge|upstream` and `X-Edge-Retry-Id: <uuid>` when it itself initiates a retry or resumes a stream. 2) add `X-Edge-Retry-Trace: <short-b64>` that encodes upstream_id + route + attempt-count so consumers/ops can correlate.
Priya Nair: add a per-tenant `Retry-Budget` concept enforced at edge: header `Edge-Retry-Budget: <n>` is not outbound but an internal counter. If budget exhausted, gateway should return 429 with `Retry-After` and a JSON explaining budget exhausted. That prevents uncontrolled hedging during incidents.
Omar Khan: operational constraints: we still can't buffer big streaming bodies. Accept gateway-origin resumes only when resume token or small body buffered. Gateway should treat requests with same `X-Edge-Retry-Id` as the same logical request for billing/metrics. For hedged client duplicates, the origin will be `client|hedge` and services can choose to dedupe by `X-Edge-Retry-Id` if present, otherwise rely on Idempotency-Key.
Carlos Mendez: concrete behavior proposal: 1) Header-only pre-commit retries: gateway coalesces if Idempotency-Key or same conn id. 2) Mid-stream client replay without Idempotency-Key: return 409 or 425 (we need bikeshed) with body {"error":"retry_requires_idempotency","hint":"attach-Idempotency-Key-or-use-resume_token"}. 3) When gateway initiates retry/resume, it sets `X-Edge-Retry-Origin: gateway`, `X-Edge-Retry-Id: uuid`, `X-Edge-Retry-Trace: base64(route,attempts,timestamp)`, and `X-Edge-Retry-TTL: 30`. 4) If tenant retry budget would be exceeded by a gateway retry, return 429: sample:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 10
X-Edge-Retry-Budget-Remaining: 0

{"error":"retry_budget_exhausted","docs":"https://docs.redwood.ai/edge/retries#budget"}
```
Sasha Ivanov: metrics to add: `edge.retry.origin.{gateway,client,hedge,upstream}`, `edge.retry.budget.exhausted`, `edge.retry.id_reused`, and `edge.retry.rejected_midstream_no_idempotency`. Logs include retry_id and trace to ease forensics.
Priya Nair: config knobs: per-tenant retry budget, per-route allowlist for resumable streams, TTL for retry-id state (default 30s), max-resume-states per-tenant. Billing note: treat same `X-Edge-Retry-Id` as single logical request when calculating chargeback.
Omar Khan: SDK guidance: 1) avoid client hedging for streaming bodies unless SDK supports resume tokens or Idempotency-Key. 2) on 429 with `retry_budget_exhausted`, back off and surface clear message to user. 3) when a gateway returns `X-Edge-Retry-Id`, SDKs can surface it for tracing.
Carlos Mendez: test plan: unit tests for header propagation and budget enforcement, integration test simulating hedging + gateway retry with resume token and without, and load test to validate budget throttling and GC of retry state. I'll draft the RFC addendum with token format, header semantics, sample curl flows, and migration path for SDKs. Tagging eng/runtime, eng-platform, and product for review.
ops-bot: rollout queued: feature/edge-retry-budget-and-trace — CI passed :white_check_mark:
Meera Patel: one last note: pick stable header names (we used both X-Edge- and X-RW- in other threads). Let's consolidate to `X-RW-Retry-*` in RFC so we don't proliferate names. Good work team.
